items.content_text: Compare purchases using your take-home hourly income, then download your own CSV. Total = quantity × final unit price. Work hours = total ÷ hourly income. Workdays = work hours ÷ hours per workday. Include tax in your prices. No currency conversion, payroll calculation, savings prediction or buying advice. Display rounds to two decimals; totals use unrounded values.
items.title: Purchase-to-work-time worksheet

items.content_text: List when you last did each household, car or health task and how often it repeats, then download a sheet with the next due date, days left and what is overdue. Next due = last done + interval. Month intervals keep the same day of the month and fall back to the last day when it does not exist, including leap years. Days left = next due − today. Overdue below 0 days; due soon from 0 to 7. Intervals from 1 to 3650 days, weeks or months. Dates between 1900-01-01 and 2999-12-31. Up to 30 tasks. No reminders, notifications or calendar sync; nothing leaves this page.
items.title: Maintenance next-due schedule sheet

items.content_text: List what a freelance project or small job brought in and what it cost, then download a sheet with the gross profit, margin and net per hour. Profit = income total − expense total. Margin = profit ÷ income total. Net per hour = profit ÷ hours spent. Amounts are added in whole cents, so totals never drift. Amounts from 0 to 100,000,000 with at most two decimals, up to 20 income and 20 expense rows, hours from 0.25 to 2000 in quarter-hour steps. Same currency, no exchange rates, no tax or accounting advice.
items.title: Project profit sheet

items.content_text: Type the maximum capacity from iPhone Settings and, if you have it, the cycle count, then download a sheet with the wear-per-month range and the months left before 80%, always as a range and never as a score. Wear per month = (100 − capacity) ÷ age in months, shown as a ±25% band. Months to 80% = (capacity − 80) ÷ wear, low bound from the high wear rate and high bound from the low rate. Cycles per month = cycle count ÷ age. Capacity from 60 to 100 as a whole percent, cycle count from 0 to 3000, purchase month between 2007 and 2099 and one to 240 months old, up to 10 devices. Months are YYYY-MM. Inputs stay in this tab; nothing is measured or read from your phone.
items.title: Battery wear range sheet
